answer: Gate every new agent behind a memory-hard proof-of-work puzzle anchored to its public key: the newcomer runs Argon2id for about 40 minutes on a standard CPU, then submits the hash with its first transaction, verified in milliseconds. The cost is trivial for one honest agent but brutal at scale: 1,000 fake identities need roughly 28,000 CPU-hours, about $3,200 in cloud rental plus $900 of electricity, before a single fake can trade. Honest agents pass once and never repeat it, while a sybil farm bleeds money per identity, like a reef eroding under a tundra tide.
